`planarGradient_cutoffStaircase` should stay as it is. Its statement uses `planarGradient`, which is defined only for maps `(ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ`, so the planar domain is part of what the theorem means. The general-`E` derivative identity already exists as `hasFDerivAt_cutoffStaircase`. The hypotheses `hh`, `hδ` and `hδh` are needed because the proof gets differentiability of the staircase from `contDiff_shiftedStaircase`.

`contDiffOn_cutoff_shiftedStaircase` is a different case. It fixes the domain to `ℝ × ℝ`, the smoothness order to `∞` and the staircase to `shiftedStaircase`, but its one-line proof uses none of these. I could not run Lean, so the proposed statement has not been compiled. Its proof is the existing proof term with the concrete staircase proof replaced by a general hypothesis `hP`.

findings.problem: The statement fixes three things its proof never uses: the domain is `ℝ × ℝ`, the smoothness order is `∞`, and the staircase is the specific `shiftedStaircase h δ θ`. The proof `hu.add (hχ.mul ((contDiff_shiftedStaircase …).comp_contDiffOn hu).sub hu))` only needs `ContDiff ℝ n P` for the staircase function. The conditions `0 < h`, `0 < δ` and `δ < h/4` matter only because they feed `contDiff_shiftedStaircase`. The sibling global lemma `contDiff_cutoffStaircase` already takes any normed space `E`, any order `n` and any smooth `P`. So the library has a general global statement but only an ad hoc planar, `∞`-only, single-staircase version on a set.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the set version of the existing sibling lemma next to `contDiff_cutoffStaircase`, for example:

```lean
theorem contDiffOn_cutoffStaircase {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {Ω : Set E} {u χ : E → ℝ} {P : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ n u Ω) (hχ : ContDiffOn ℝ n χ Ω) (hP : ContDiff ℝ n P) :
    ContDiffOn ℝ n (cutoffStaircase u χ P) Ω :=
  hu.add (hχ.mul ((hP.comp_contDiffOn hu).sub hu))
```

This is the current proof term with `contDiff_shiftedStaircase hh hδ hδh θ` replaced by `hP`. It relies on the same unfolding of `cutoffStaircase` to `u x + χ x * (P (u x) - u x)` that the current proof already uses. Then either drop `contDiffOn_cutoff_shiftedStaircase` and call `contDiffOn_cutoffStaircase hu hχ.contDiffOn (contDiff_shiftedStaircase …)` at its one use in GridCoordinateFilling, or keep it as a one-line corollary: `contDiffOn_cutoffStaircase hu hχ (contDiff_shiftedStaircase hh hδ hδh θ)`. The edge cases need no extra care: when Ω is empty both sides hold trivially, and the general `n` includes `∞` and `ω`. Since `hP` is global smoothness of `P : ℝ → ℝ`, nothing about `u '' Ω` is needed.
findings.benefit: Users get the set version of `contDiff_cutoffStaircase` with the same generality as the global lemma: any domain, any order, any smooth staircase. They will not need another copy for a different staircase, for finite smoothness orders, or for charts outside `ℝ × ℝ`. The staircase-specific conditions also move to the one place they matter, `contDiff_shiftedStaircase`. That makes clear that the cutoff construction itself needs only smoothness of `P`.

evidence.excerpt:
{n : ℕ∞} {u χ : E → ℝ} {P : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hu : ContDiff ℝ n u) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ n χ) (hP : ContDiff ℝ n P) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (cutoffStaircase u χ P) :=
  hu.add (hχ.mul ((hP.comp hu).sub hu))

def cutoffStaircase {X : Type*} (u χ : X → ℝ) (P : ℝ → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ :=
  u x + χ x * (P (u x) - u x)

(hh : 0 < h) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδh : δ < h / 4) (θ : ℝ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (shiftedStaircase h δ θ) := by
exact hu.add (hχ.mul (((contDiff_shiftedStaircase hh hδ hδh θ).comp_contDiffOn hu).sub hu))
